From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Overall position

The Seller’s package shifts several deal-critical risks to Wattlebridge while seeking broad liability protection. We should reject the proposed “one-size-fits-all” limitations regime and require specific completion deliverables, targeted indemnities and price protection for identified risks.

## Principal push-backs

### 1. Liability regime is too broad

**Seller position:** 20% cap (AUD 4.8m), AUD 25,000 de minimis, AUD 250,000 deductible basket, 18-month survival, with all limitations extended to all claims.

**Buyer concern:** This would materially dilute the value of the warranties and could leave the Buyer without meaningful recourse for title, tax, IP ownership, data/privacy, debt, fraud and known specific risks.

**Push back:**
- Limit the 20% cap, basket and de minimis to ordinary business warranties only.
- Make the basket **tipping/first-dollar**, rather than deductible, or reduce it substantially. At minimum, losses should be recoverable in full once the threshold is exceeded.
- Exclude from the de minimis/basket:
  - title, capacity and authority;
  - tax;
  - IP ownership/infringement and the Ironquay matter;
  - fraud, wilful misconduct, deliberate concealment and breach of covenant;
  - indemnity claims and leakage/Completion adjustments;
  - the Riverlark facility/security;
  - privacy, cyber and regulatory matters.
- Extend general warranty survival to at least 24 months. Tax claims should survive through the relevant statutory assessment period plus a buffer; title, capacity, fraud and deliberate concealment should have a materially higher cap and longer period (or no contractual limit, subject to the long-stop limitation law).
- Resist any clause purporting to restrict mandatory statutory rights.

### 2. Title and fundamental warranties must not be under the general regime

**Seller position:** Title and capacity subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month period “for administrative simplicity.”

**Buyer concern:** Wattlebridge is purchasing 100% ownership and control. Title, power and no-encumbrance risk is fundamentally different from ordinary operational warranty risk.

**Push back:**
- Title, capacity, authority and valid issue of shares should be uncapped or capped at 100% of purchase price, with a much longer survival period.
- Require warranties that:
  - Harbourglass owns the shares beneficially and legally;
  - they are fully paid, free of all security interests, options, pre-emptive rights and third-party claims;
  - there are no undisclosed agreements affecting voting, transfer or economic rights;
  - Completion transfers good title to Wattlebridge.
- DD-012 is evidence only; it is not a substitute for a substantive title warranty and Completion delivery package.

### 3. General data-room and public-record disclosure should be rejected

**Seller position:** Every matter “contained or referred to” in the data room, statutory registers and public records is generally disclosed.

**Buyer concern:** This is an impermissibly broad disclosure standard. It requires the Buyer to identify and assess every implication from a large body of material, including cross-document inferences and incomplete materials.

**Push back:**
- Delete general disclosure of the data room, public registers and public records.
- Disclosure should qualify warranties only where it is:
  - specifically identified against the relevant warranty;
  - fair, clear, accurate and sufficiently detailed to identify the nature, scope and reasonably foreseeable consequences of the matter;
  - included in an agreed disclosure bundle/index frozen at signing.
- No disclosure by implication, cross-reference, documents “referred to”, public searches, or matters merely discoverable through investigation.
- Specific disclosure should not qualify a warranty where the disclosure itself identifies missing facts, absent consents, unresolved conditions or incomplete investigation.

### 4. Buyer knowledge exclusion is unacceptable in its proposed form

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.

**Buyer concern:** This effectively replaces the agreed warranty allocation with a due-diligence standard and imputes knowledge from advisers to Wattlebridge.

**Push back:**
- Delete constructive knowledge and “discoverable” knowledge.
- If a knowledge qualifier is unavoidable, confine it to Wattlebridge’s actual knowledge, as at signing, of named senior deal-team members only, from written information expressly identified as qualifying the relevant warranty.
- Do not impute adviser knowledge, consultant knowledge, knowledge acquired after signing, or knowledge inferred from an incomplete disclosure.
- Preserve claims for fraud, deliberate concealment, misleading statements and breach of covenant regardless of Buyer knowledge.

## Identified transaction risks

### 5. Bluefen: 30% of FY26 revenue; consent must be a genuine Completion condition

**Facts:** Bluefen represented approximately AUD 3.6m / 30% of FY26 revenue. The change-of-control consent has conditions, and neither final written consent nor evidence of satisfaction is included.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours and condition satisfied upon delivery of written consent.

**Buyer concern:** A consent that remains conditional, or can be withdrawn/not operative because conditions are unsatisfied, does not protect the business or revenue base.

**Push back:**
- Make valid Bluefen consent a Buyer-benefit Completion condition.
- Consent must be unconditional, irrevocable and effective at Completion, or all conditions must be expressly waived or satisfied before Completion.
- Require no termination, suspension, price reduction, adverse amendment, release, waiver or new obligation under the Bluefen contract.
- Require a specific warranty and indemnity for loss arising from breach, termination, non-renewal, adverse variation or invalidity of the consent.
- Wattlebridge should retain a walk right if this is not achieved by the agreed long-stop date.

### 6. Riverlark debt and security must be discharged at or before Completion

**Facts:** Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; no repayment or security discharge is in the data room.

**Seller position:** A release will be provided “following Completion.”

**Buyer concern:** The agreed transaction is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release creates a period in which the acquired company remains indebted and/or encumbered, and exposes Wattlebridge to enforcement and operational restrictions.

**Push back:**
- Riverlark debt must be repaid at or immediately before Completion from Seller proceeds.
- Obtain, as Completion deliverables:
  - payoff letter stating final amount;
  - executed releases/discharges of all guarantees and security;
  - authority to lodge PPSR releases;
  - evidence that releases have been lodged promptly after Completion.
- The Completion funds flow must separately show the debt repayment and discharge mechanics.
- If any release cannot legally be delivered at Completion, retain an agreed amount in escrow/holdback and give Wattlebridge a termination/withholding right.

### 7. Completion bonuses are undisclosed leakage/debt-like items

**Facts:** DD-005 identifies AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses, not included in funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and other employment on-costs are not addressed.

**Buyer concern:** Completion-triggered employee bonuses economically arise from the sale and should not become a post-Completion Company cost borne by Wattlebridge, particularly under a debt-free/cash-free deal.

**Push back:**
- Treat all Completion bonuses and all associated superannuation, payroll tax, leave impacts, administration costs and other on-costs as:
  - Seller leakage, or
  - debt-like items deducted dollar-for-dollar from price, with agreed gross-up for on-costs.
- Require a detailed employee-by-employee schedule and full quantified amount before signing/Completion.
- Seller should pay or procure payment at Completion, and indemnify Wattlebridge/the Company for all related liabilities.
- Ensure post-Completion continued-employment conditions do not transfer a Seller sale-related obligation to the Buyer. If Seller insists, price protection or escrow is required.

### 8. Ironquay IP risk requires broader protection

**Facts:** SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; AUD 180,000 remains recorded as open; no evidence of payment or confirmatory assignment exists.

**Seller position:** Indemnity restricted to the SOW3 payment.

**Buyer concern:** Payment alone does not establish that Paperbark owns or can use the relevant IP. Risk includes non-assignment, incomplete deliverables, retained rights, infringement, claims, disruption and costs of replacement/remediation.

**Push back:**
- Require before Completion:
  - evidence of full payment;
  - executed assignment/confirmatory assignment of all relevant IP and deliverables;
  - waivers/consents for moral rights where applicable;
  - confirmation that no lien, security interest or retained ownership claim exists;
  - rights sufficient for Paperbark’s present and anticipated business.
- Alternatively, obtain a separate uncapped or appropriately ring-fenced indemnity, plus an escrow/holdback materially exceeding AUD 180,000 to cover replacement, re-performance, claims and business interruption.
- IP title, non-infringement and sufficiency warranties should be outside the general warranty cap/basket/time limit.

### 9. Export/privacy incident is not adequately addressed

**Facts:** A download link may have exposed approximately 1,240 personal-information records to an unintended external address. Investigation is preliminary and neither access nor notification requirements are resolved.

**Seller position:** It is “not expected to be material.”

**Buyer concern:** This is unresolved regulatory, customer, remediation and reputational exposure. The fact that the investigation is incomplete is a reason for protection, not a reason to minimise the issue.

**Push back:**
- Require a complete incident report before Completion, including data categories, recipients, access-log evidence, containment, deletion confirmation, legal advice on notification, affected-person/customer exposure and remediation plan.
- Require compliance with all applicable privacy, data-security, contractual and regulatory notification obligations.
- Obtain a specific indemnity for all pre-Completion incident losses, including investigation, legal advice, notification, remediation, regulator engagement, customer claims, penalties to the extent legally indemnifiable, and third-party costs.
- Consider a separate escrow/holdback pending closure of the investigation.
- Add a Completion covenant preventing deletion or alteration of evidence and requiring ongoing cooperation after Completion.

### 10. Other disclosed contracts require verification, not assumptions

**Office lease:** DD-007’s notification obligation must be reviewed. Confirm whether notice, consent, information delivery, lender approval or other consequences arise from the share sale. Require all necessary notices/consents by Completion and a no-default warranty.

**Sandbar supplier renewals:** AUD 330,000 may be ordinary course, but that conclusion cannot be assumed. Require the contracts, renewal notices, termination rights, payment terms, service scope, budget treatment and confirmation whether the costs are accrued, prepaid or avoidable. Exclude unusual/prepaid/non-ordinary amounts from the debt-free/cash-free calculation or treat them as leakage.

**Mossvale:** The disclosure’s assertion that assignment restrictions do not apply to a share sale is not determinative. Review the actual wording for change-of-control, indirect transfer, control or analogous provisions. Obtain consent if required or commercially prudent.

## Tax and price-mechanics protections

The Seller’s statement that tax is “settled under the general regime” should be rejected.

**Push back:**
- Include a standalone tax covenant and tax indemnity for all pre-Completion taxes, including tax arising from pre-Completion transactions or the sale process.
- Tax claims should not be subject to the general cap, basket, de minimis or 18-month period.
- Ensure debt-free/cash-free definitions capture all debt-like amounts, including accrued interest, bank fees, unpaid bonuses and on-costs, security-release costs, unpaid supplier liabilities where appropriate, and transaction costs borne by the Company.
- Require an agreed Completion statement, robust post-Completion true-up, and audit/access rights.

## Remedies and non-reliance

**Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims of any nature.

**Push back:**
- Restrict exclusive remedy language to contractual warranty claims only, and only to the extent expressly agreed.
- Preserve remedies for fraud, fraudulent or negligent misrepresentation where legally permissible, deliberate concealment, breach of covenant, specific indemnities, equitable relief and statutory rights.
- Do not give a broad non-reliance acknowledgement that could undermine the Buyer’s ability to rely on express SPA warranties or disclosure accuracy.
- Seller should warrant that disclosures and information supplied are not misleading or deceptive by statement or omission, subject to appropriately negotiated qualifications.

## Recommended negotiating priorities

1. **Bluefen consent**: unconditional/effective consent and satisfaction of all conditions as a Completion condition; walk right and specific indemnity.  
2. **Riverlark**: repayment and security release at Completion, not afterwards.  
3. **Price protection**: deduct or treat as leakage the AUD 420,000 bonuses plus all on-costs; fully identify debt-like and transaction-related liabilities.  
4. **Ironquay**: prove payment and obtain IP assignment/confirmation, or substantial ring-fenced indemnity and holdback.  
5. **Privacy incident**: complete investigation, remediation and specific indemnity/escrow.  
6. **Liability architecture**: retain ordinary-warranty limitations only; carve out title, tax, IP, indemnities, fraud, covenants, debt/leakage and identified issues.  
7. **Disclosure/knowledge**: remove blanket data-room/public-record disclosure and constructive Buyer knowledge.  
8. **Contract diligence**: verify lease, Sandbar and Mossvale provisions from the operative documents and obtain required consents/notices.

The Seller’s disclosure letter is useful in identifying risk areas, but it should not operate as a blanket waiver of warranties or as an acceptance that incomplete information, absent evidence and unresolved investigations have been adequately disclosed.

6. **Liability architecture**: retain ordinary-warranty limitations only; carve out title, tax, IP, indemnities, fraud, covenants, debt/leakage and identified issues.  
7. **Disclosure/knowledge**: remove blanket data-room/public-record disclosure and constructive Buyer knowledge.  
8. **Contract diligence**: verify lease, Sandbar and Mossvale provisions from the operative documents and obtain required consents/notices.

The Seller’s disclosure letter is useful in identifying risk areas, but it should not operate as a blanket waiver of warranties or as an acceptance that incomplete information, absent evidence and unresolved investigations have been adequately disclosed.
